question: GQ-007
subject: 777 books, and a guard that checked presence instead of completeness

fifth_list_complete.five_lists_total: every failure transient, not one book permanently unavailable

the_defect.symptom: long_s_passages fell from 160,175 to 53,517 while the corpus GREW
the_defect.cause: passage_modern held 334,000 rows against 981,260 passages — the modern-spelling build was cut short
the_defect.why_the_pipeline_said_success: the guard checked that the TABLE EXISTS, not that it is complete
the_defect.the_irony: I added exactly this presence-versus-completeness check to the passage index earlier in this same run, and missed it one step later

root_cause: add-longs-variants now exceeds a ten-minute call at 981,260 passages — the same threshold the rebuild crossed
fix: the pipeline now compares passage_modern rows against passage_ext rows and exits 1 on a mismatch
a_number_that_would_have_been_published: long_s_passages 53,517 would have gone onto the observatory and the library page as fact. A count that FELL while the corpus grew is the kind of number a reader would have trusted.

root_cause_measured.first_hypothesis: the build simply exceeds ten minutes
root_cause_measured.why: limit/offset makes sqlite walk every skipped row; across 490 batches the tail costs hours
root_cause_measured.fix: rowid-range paging — an FTS5 table has an implicit rowid, so a range scan is constant-cost per batch
root_cause_measured.the_general_lesson: the fix for a slow query is usually an index-shaped query, not a smaller batch — the same finding as the passage index count(*)

a_recovery_that_worked.symptom: "attempt to write a readonly database (8)" from a read-only connection
a_recovery_that_worked.cause: a 5.6 MB rollback journal left by the process killed at the ten-minute timeout
a_recovery_that_worked.why_read_only_fails: sqlite must REPLAY the journal to open the database, and a read-only connection cannot
a_recovery_that_worked.recovery: opened writable, sqlite replayed it — 454,000 rows preserved, passage_ext intact at 981,260, journal cleared
a_recovery_that_worked.verdict: no data loss. The rollback journal did exactly its job.
